world.title: Huge crowds in Mashhad as Iran's late supreme leader is buried
world.summary: Ali Khamenei, Iran's supreme leader, was buried at the Imam Reza shrine in Mashhad, Iran's holiest Shia Muslim site, concluding six days of public mourning ceremonies. The burial marked the end of an extended period of national mourning following Khamenei's death. The Imam Reza shrine, located in northeastern Iran, holds profound religious significance for Shia Muslims worldwide. Khamenei's death and subsequent funeral proceedings represent a major political transition for Iran, as the supreme leader holds the highest authority in the Islamic Republic's governmental structure. The massive attendance at the burial underscores the significant role Khamenei held in Iranian society and politics.

world.title: China lands reusable rocket for first time, state media says
world.summary: China successfully landed a reusable rocket for the first time, according to state media reports, marking a significant milestone in the nation's space program development. This achievement follows similar technological accomplishments by US-owned companies SpaceX and Blue Origin, which have previously demonstrated reusable rocket landing capabilities. The development of reusable rocket technology represents a major advancement in reducing space launch costs and increasing the frequency of space missions. China's success in this area demonstrates the country's growing capabilities in aerospace engineering and its commitment to competing in the commercial space industry. The milestone reflects broader international competition in space exploration and the increasing accessibility of space technology.

world.title: Big fall in oil, gas and cargo ships taking US-backed Hormuz route after new strikes
world.summary: Data indicates a significant decline in the number of ships, many carrying oil and gas, transiting through the Hormuz Strait following recent attacks this week. The Hormuz Strait, a critical waterway for global energy supplies, has experienced reduced traffic as shipping companies reassess security risks. The attacks prompted vessels to avoid the US-backed route, potentially disrupting international energy markets and trade flows. This decline reflects heightened tensions in the region and concerns about maritime security. The reduction in shipping through this strategic chokepoint has implications for global oil prices and energy security, as the Hormuz Strait is one of the world's most important petroleum transit routes, with millions of barrels passing through daily.

world.title: Ukraine strikes Russian ships near Crimea, escalating attacks on fuel supplies
world.summary: Ukraine has conducted strikes against Russian ships positioned near Crimea, representing an escalation in attacks targeting fuel supplies and logistical routes. These military operations appear to constitute the latest phase of Ukraine's strategic campaign to disrupt supply lines and restrict access to and from occupied Crimea. The attacks demonstrate Ukraine's expanding capability to project military force against Russian naval assets in the Black Sea region. By targeting fuel supplies and maritime infrastructure, Ukraine aims to weaken Russian military operational capacity and constrain resource availability to occupied territories. The escalating nature of these strikes indicates intensifying military competition in the region and reflects Ukraine's determination to degrade Russian supply chains supporting military operations in occupied areas.

world.title: Mbappe and Dembele send France into World Cup semi-finals
world.summary: Kylian Mbappe and Ousmane Dembele led France to victory over Morocco in the World Cup quarter-finals, securing France's place in the semi-finals. Mbappe recovered from having an early penalty saved to score and help France achieve a 2-0 victory, demonstrating resilience and clinical finishing. The win advances France toward potential contention for a third consecutive World Cup final appearance. Mbappe's performance, despite the missed penalty, highlighted his importance to France's tournament campaign. The quarter-final victory represents a significant achievement in France's World Cup journey, with the team continuing to demonstrate strong form throughout the tournament as they progress deeper into the competition's knockout stages.

usa.title: Thousands of TPS holders close to losing work permits after SCOTUS ruling
usa.summary: Thousands of Haitian and Syrian immigrants holding Temporary Protected Status face imminent loss of work authorization following a recent Supreme Court ruling. This development has significant implications for the U.S. labor market, particularly in healthcare where TPS holders comprise approximately 15% of noncitizen workers. The loss of work permits could exacerbate existing staffing shortages across the healthcare sector and other industries. The ruling represents a major policy shift affecting vulnerable immigrant populations who have been authorized to work in the United States under temporary protection designations.

usa.title: Interior Department say D.C.'s height limits don't apply to Trump's proposed arch
usa.summary: The Interior Department is arguing that Washington D.C.'s century-old height restrictions do not apply to federal projects, specifically regarding a proposed Trump arch monument. This position represents a significant departure from established precedent governing the nation's capital. If the reviewing panel accepts this argument, it could fundamentally alter how height regulations are enforced in D.C. and set new precedent for future federal construction projects. The debate centers on whether federal properties should be exempt from local zoning and height restrictions that have shaped the city's skyline for generations.

usa.title: What to know about 'explosive diarrhoea' parasite outbreak in US
usa.summary: A cyclosporiasis outbreak has spread across at least 17 U.S. states, causing illness characterized by severe gastrointestinal symptoms. The parasitic infection, transmitted through contaminated food or water, has affected multiple states with the source remaining unclear. Health authorities are investigating the outbreak's origin to prevent further transmission. Cyclosporiasis typically causes prolonged diarrhea and other digestive complications. The multi-state nature of the outbreak suggests a common source, possibly linked to contaminated produce or food products distributed across regions, prompting urgent public health investigation and consumer awareness efforts.

usa.title: Some Republican states push for new college accreditation agency
usa.summary: Several Republican-led states are establishing a new college accreditation agency, citing goals to increase what they characterize as intellectual diversity in higher education. This initiative represents a significant shift in educational governance, challenging the existing accreditation system that has long been dominated by traditional agencies. The new agency reflects broader political debates about curriculum content, academic freedom, and ideological balance in universities. The move could fragment higher education accreditation standards and create competing systems for evaluating institutional quality, potentially affecting student transfers, employer recognition of degrees, and federal funding eligibility for institutions.

usa.title: US officer charged after two police dogs die in hot patrol car
usa.summary: A U.S. police officer has been charged following the deaths of two drug and bomb-sniffing dogs left in a patrol car for seven hours. The incident highlights serious concerns about animal welfare and officer accountability in law enforcement. The dogs, which were working K-9 unit members, died from heat exposure in the vehicle. The charges represent a rare case of criminal accountability for animal neglect involving police personnel. The case has drawn attention to protocols for protecting working animals in law enforcement and raises questions about supervision and safety procedures within police departments.

india.title: Tensions erupt in West Bengal after 11-year-old raped and murdered
india.summary: A tragic incident in West Bengal has sparked significant tensions following the discovery of an 11-year-old girl's body in a pond. The child went missing and was reported by her family, with her body recovered a day later. This case has ignited widespread public outrage and social unrest in the region, highlighting ongoing concerns about child safety and violence against minors in India. The incident has prompted discussions about law enforcement response and community protection measures, drawing considerable media attention and public scrutiny regarding the circumstances surrounding the crime and subsequent investigation.

india.title: India is adding biofuels to petrol – but many drivers are unhappy
india.summary: India has introduced E20 fuel blend, a biofuel mixture added to petrol, but the initiative has faced significant pushback from motorists. Drivers report that the E20 fuel blend has substantially reduced their vehicles' fuel efficiency, raising concerns about increased operational costs. Additionally, consumers worry about potential higher maintenance expenses resulting from the new fuel composition. This policy shift, intended to promote renewable energy and reduce environmental impact, has created tension between government environmental objectives and consumer concerns about practical economic implications and vehicle performance in real-world driving conditions.

india.title: US prosecutors charge Indian crime boss with murder of Sikh activist in Canada
india.summary: United States prosecutors have filed charges against an Indian crime boss in connection with the murder of a Sikh activist in Canada. This prosecution represents part of a comprehensive law enforcement operation involving coordinated arrests across the United States, Canada, and Europe. The case highlights transnational organized crime networks and international cooperation between law enforcement agencies. The charges underscore serious concerns about criminal activities spanning multiple countries and jurisdictions, demonstrating efforts by authorities to combat organized crime with cross-border implications and to hold perpetrators accountable for violent crimes affecting diaspora communities.

india.title: Why an anti-sacrilege law in Punjab has sparked controversy
india.summary: Punjab's anti-sacrilege law has reignited significant controversy, reviving one of the state's most sensitive political and religious issues. The dispute carries substantial implications ahead of state elections scheduled for next year, making it a focal point for political discourse. The law addresses religious sensitivities within Punjab's diverse population, but its implementation and interpretation have generated considerable debate among various stakeholder groups. The controversy reflects broader tensions between religious protection measures and secular governance principles, with political parties positioning themselves differently on the issue. This contentious matter is expected to influence electoral dynamics and political campaigns in the upcoming state elections.

india.title: Instagram running ads promoting child sexual abuse material in India, BBC finds
india.summary: The BBC has uncovered a disturbing situation where Instagram is running advertisements that promote child sexual abuse material in India. These advertisements employ explicit terminology including references to rape and child exploitation, with links directing users to content hosted on the messaging application Telegram. This discovery reveals a serious gap in content moderation and platform safety mechanisms, exposing vulnerable populations to harmful material. The findings highlight significant concerns about social media platform accountability, the effectiveness of existing safeguarding protocols, and the need for stronger enforcement of policies protecting children from exploitation and abuse online.

odisha.title: How an Odisha Town Turned Old Waste Vehicles Into Art, History & a Public Park
odisha.summary: Rayagada in Odisha has transformed discarded waste vehicles and materials into a unique public park, demonstrating innovative waste management and sustainability practices. What would have ended up in scrapyards has been repurposed into meaningful art installations and historical exhibits, creating a destination that attracts visitors while reducing landfill burden. This initiative showcases how communities can address waste management challenges creatively, turning environmental problems into cultural and recreational assets. The project reflects growing efforts in Odisha to promote circular economy principles and sustainable development through community engagement and creative reuse of materials.

odisha.title: Beyond building homes: How Odisha is combining affordable housing with rooftop solar
odisha.summary: Odisha is integrating rooftop solar systems into its affordable housing schemes, enabling beneficiaries to acquire subsidized solar panels for their new homes. This innovative approach aims to reduce long-term electricity costs for low-income families, combining housing development with renewable energy adoption. The initiative addresses dual challenges of housing shortage and energy affordability while promoting clean energy transition. By embedding solar technology into housing programs, Odisha is helping vulnerable populations achieve energy independence and lower utility expenses, demonstrating how state-level policies can integrate sustainability with social welfare objectives.

odisha.title: The capex fault line running via Indian states: Odisha leads, Punjab lags
odisha.summary: Odisha leads Indian states in capital expenditure commitment, dedicating 6.5% of its economic output to infrastructure development, significantly outpacing states like Punjab and Kerala. While Odisha prioritizes infrastructure investment for growth, Punjab and Kerala face fiscal constraints due to welfare obligations and interest payments on existing debt. This divergence in state spending priorities reflects different development strategies and fiscal management approaches across India. Odisha's emphasis on capital expenditure positions it as a model for infrastructure-driven growth, while other states struggle with competing demands between welfare spending and development investments.

odisha.title: Maharashtra, Odisha women cash schemes drive financial autonomy, alter household spending—EAC-PM paper
odisha.summary: Research by the Economic Advisory Council to the Prime Minister reveals that women cash transfer schemes in Maharashtra and Odisha significantly enhance financial autonomy and alter household spending patterns. In Maharashtra, male relatives of beneficiaries spend 49% less monthly while saving 23% more, while women's own spending increases by 46%. Odisha demonstrates similar trends with reduced male spending. These findings indicate that direct cash transfers to women create measurable economic behavioral changes, promoting financial independence and shifting household resource allocation. The schemes demonstrate effectiveness in empowering women economically and reshaping family financial dynamics.

odisha.title: Odisha to intensify TB screening in 13,271 high-risk villages
odisha.summary: The Odisha government is launching an intensive tuberculosis screening drive across 13,271 high-risk villages and urban wards under the TB Mukt Bharat Abhiyan-100 Day Campaign 2.0. The initiative emphasizes X-ray-based screening to identify tuberculosis cases in vulnerable populations. This targeted approach focuses on areas with historically higher TB prevalence, aiming to improve early detection and treatment outcomes. The campaign represents Odisha's commitment to achieving tuberculosis elimination goals through systematic screening and intervention in high-risk communities, strengthening public health infrastructure and disease surveillance mechanisms across rural and urban areas.

sports.title: Dybantsa outduels Peterson in Las Vegas debut
sports.summary: AJ Dybantsa, the 2026 NBA Draft's No. 1 overall pick, led all scorers with 27 points in his Las Vegas Summer League debut, powering the Washington Wizards to victory over the Utah Jazz and No. 2 pick Darryn Peterson. The matchup between the top two draft prospects provided an early showcase of the league's newest talent, with Dybantsa's dominant performance establishing him as a significant contributor for the Wizards. The Summer League serves as a crucial evaluation period for draft picks to demonstrate their NBA-readiness and develop chemistry with their new teams before the regular season begins.

sports.title: Mbappé allays WC injury concern: 'I'm all good'
sports.summary: Kylian Mbappé downplayed injury concerns following France's 2-0 World Cup quarterfinal victory over Morocco, describing the issue as merely a "knock on his ankle." The French superstar's reassurance comes as a relief to France's World Cup campaign, as Mbappé has been instrumental in their tournament run. His availability is crucial for France's semifinal prospects, as the team is considered among the favorites to win the 2026 World Cup. Mbappé's continued fitness will be essential for France's pursuit of their third World Cup title.

sports.title: Clips-Raptors trade for Kawhi on hold amid probe
sports.summary: The proposed trade between the Los Angeles Clippers and Toronto Raptors involving star player Kawhi Leonard has been placed on hold pending completion of an NBA investigation into whether the Clippers circumvented salary cap regulations. The investigation's outcome will determine whether the trade can proceed as planned. This development adds uncertainty to the offseason transaction and highlights the league's commitment to enforcing salary cap compliance. The delay affects both franchises' roster construction plans and their ability to finalize their rosters ahead of the upcoming season.

sports.title: Eight indicted in thwarted attack on UFC's WH event
sports.summary: A federal grand jury indicted eight men Thursday for their alleged roles in a thwarted drone and sniper attack targeting the UFC Freedom 250 event held at the White House in June. The indictments represent a significant development in the investigation into the security threat against the high-profile sporting event. The foiled attack underscores ongoing security concerns surrounding major public events and the coordination required between law enforcement and event organizers. The case highlights the serious nature of threats against prominent sporting venues and the federal government's commitment to prosecuting those involved in such plots.

sports.title: Arthur Fery reaches Wimbledon semi-finals as British wildcard
sports.summary: British wildcard Arthur Fery has advanced to the Wimbledon semi-finals, achieving a remarkable feat in his tournament run. Fery learned to play tennis approximately one mile from Wimbledon's Centre Court and has now reached the final stages of the prestigious tournament. His journey from local player to semi-finalist represents an inspiring story of perseverance and talent development. Fery is now just one victory away from reaching the Wimbledon final, continuing his remarkable run at the historic grass-court championship where he earned his wildcard entry.

cricket.title: Brook and Salt blow India away as England romp to series win
cricket.summary: England secured a series victory against India with strong performances from Brook and Salt, with Indian batter Iyer scoring an unbeaten 80 but lacking support as England bowlers Archer and Tongue took key wickets. This victory comes as part of England's recent strong run of form in international cricket. The win demonstrates England's competitive strength in the current cricket landscape and marks a significant achievement in their bilateral series against India.

cricket.title: India and England turn to whites as Lord's gears up for a historic first
cricket.summary: India and England are preparing for a historic one-off Test match at Lord's, marking a significant milestone in women's cricket. Both teams are transitioning quickly from the T20 World Cup to this Test format encounter. With over 30,000 tickets already sold, the occasion promises to be a landmark event. The match represents growing momentum for women's Test cricket, with players like Harmanpreet and Sciver-Brunt advocating for more Test opportunities. This fixture underscores the increasing prominence and investment in women's cricket at the international level.

cricket.title: Curran and Ngarava seal Zimbabwe's stunning series win
cricket.summary: Zimbabwe achieved a stunning series victory over Bangladesh, with Curran and Ngarava playing crucial roles in securing the win. Bangladesh collapsed dramatically during their chase of 248, losing seven wickets for just 65 runs in the second ODI to lose both the match and the series. This upset victory represents a significant achievement for Zimbabwe in international cricket, demonstrating their competitive capability against established teams. The collapse highlighted Bangladesh's batting vulnerabilities in pressure situations during the series.

cricket.title: Mustafizur Rahman ruled out for four weeks with hamstring and knee injuries
cricket.summary: Bangladesh fast bowler Mustafizur Rahman has been ruled out for four weeks due to hamstring and knee injuries, forcing him to miss the remainder of Bangladesh's tour of Zimbabwe. This injury represents a significant blow to Bangladesh's bowling attack during a critical period of their international schedule. The loss of a key pace bowler impacts Bangladesh's ability to compete effectively in upcoming matches. Such injuries highlight the physical demands placed on cricketers during intensive touring schedules and the importance of injury management in international cricket.

cricket.title: Ashwin ruled out of rest of MLC 2026 with knee injury
cricket.summary: Indian spinner Ravichandran Ashwin has been ruled out of the remainder of the Major League Cricket 2026 tournament due to a knee injury. Australian fast bowler Peter Siddle has been approved as his replacement, bringing international experience to the franchise. Ashwin's absence represents a significant loss for his team, as he is a key player in the MLC competition. The injury underscores the challenges of managing player fitness across multiple cricket formats and tournaments occurring simultaneously during the international cricket calendar.

usa_stock.title: SK Hynix raises $26.5 billion in U.S. offering. What to know about the stock.
usa_stock.summary: SK Hynix, a major South Korean memory chip manufacturer, is conducting a significant $26.5 billion offering to U.S. investors, marking an important entry point for American market participants into the semiconductor sector. This offering provides investors with a direct opportunity to gain exposure to the red-hot memory chip market, which has been experiencing substantial growth and investor interest. The deal represents a major capital raise and reflects strong demand for semiconductor exposure among U.S. institutional and retail investors seeking to participate in the ongoing chip industry expansion.

usa_stock.title: Meta's stock rebounds as agentic AI coding and custom chips ease spending fears
usa_stock.summary: Meta Platforms' stock rallied on Thursday following announcements regarding a new artificial intelligence model and significant progress on custom chip development. The market had previously expressed concerns about the company's substantial capital expenditures related to AI infrastructure. The positive developments in agentic AI coding capabilities and custom chip milestones appear to have alleviated investor worries about spending efficiency and return on investment. This rebound reflects renewed confidence in Meta's strategic direction and its ability to leverage proprietary technology to manage costs while advancing its AI capabilities.

usa_stock.title: Why a hidden divergence between the VIX and Nasdaq volatility has the smart money on edge
usa_stock.summary: Market analysts have identified a concerning divergence between the VIX volatility index and Nasdaq-specific volatility measures, signaling potential market instability despite the ongoing bull market rally. While traders remain enthusiastic about equity gains, particularly in technology stocks, the elevated volatility in Nasdaq-listed securities suggests underlying market stress that may warrant defensive positioning. This technical divergence has prompted sophisticated investors to consider hedging strategies to protect against potential downside risk, indicating that despite surface-level market strength, professional money managers are taking precautions against unforeseen market corrections.

usa_stock.title: Can Walmart help the Fed harness real-time U.S. economic data? We're about to find out.
usa_stock.summary: The Federal Reserve has appointed a former Walmart CEO to lead a task force focused on developing real-time economic data collection and analysis capabilities. This initiative aims to provide policymakers with contemporaneous information on consumer spending patterns, inflation trends, and economic growth metrics. By leveraging Walmart's extensive retail operations and data infrastructure, the Federal Reserve seeks to obtain more timely economic indicators than traditional government statistics allow. This collaboration represents an innovative approach to monetary policy decision-making, potentially enabling faster policy responses to emerging economic conditions.

usa_stock.title: Bidding war breaks out for easyJet as Apollo tops rival private-equity group's bid
usa_stock.summary: A competitive bidding war has emerged for easyJet, the British low-cost airline, with Apollo Global Management submitting a bid that surpasses a rival American private-equity firm's offer. The escalating auction reflects strong investor appetite for the airline sector and easyJet's strategic value as a major European carrier. Multiple private-equity groups competing for the acquisition indicates confidence in the company's operational potential and market position. This bidding competition is likely to drive up the final acquisition price, benefiting current shareholders while demonstrating continued private-equity interest in consolidating the airline industry.

ai.title: Anthropic found a hidden space where Claude puzzles over concepts
ai.summary: Anthropic has developed a technique called the Jacobian lens that provides unprecedented insight into how large language models process information internally. The tool reveals what occurs within AI systems as they answer questions and perform tasks, uncovering findings that range from mundane to concerning. This breakthrough represents the clearest glimpse yet into the inner workings of LLMs, offering researchers a window into the mechanisms underlying AI decision-making and reasoning processes. The discovery has significant implications for understanding and potentially improving AI transparency and interpretability.

ai.title: OpenAI wants its new tool to do your work for you and with you
ai.summary: OpenAI has rebranded its Codex tool to offer independent workflows capable of running autonomously for extended periods. The new tool is designed to both perform work independently and collaborate with users on tasks. This represents a significant evolution in AI assistants, moving beyond simple query-response interactions toward more sophisticated autonomous operation. The capability to sustain workflows for hours without interruption marks a substantial advancement in practical AI application, potentially transforming how professionals approach complex, multi-step projects and enabling more seamless human-AI collaboration in workplace environments.

ai.title: Humanoid robots controlled by surgeons did world-first operation on live pigs
ai.summary: Surgeons have successfully controlled humanoid robots to perform a world-first surgical operation on live pigs in a preclinical trial. This groundbreaking achievement demonstrates the feasibility of deploying humanoid robots in surgical settings under human guidance. The experiment represents a critical milestone in medical robotics, testing whether advanced robotic systems can effectively assist or perform complex surgical procedures. The successful operation on living subjects suggests potential future applications in human surgery, though further development and validation will be necessary before clinical implementation in human patients.

ai.title: Hackers can use 9 of the most popular AI tools to assemble massive botnets
ai.summary: Security researchers have discovered that hackers can exploit nine of the most widely-used AI tools to construct large-scale botnets through a technique called "HalluSquatting." This attack method weaponizes a fundamental limitation of large language models—their tendency to generate plausible-sounding but false information when uncertain. By exploiting this hallucination vulnerability, attackers can manipulate AI systems into providing instructions for botnet assembly. The discovery reveals a significant security risk across popular AI platforms, highlighting how AI's inherent weaknesses can be weaponized for malicious purposes and threatening the security infrastructure of organizations relying on these tools.

ai.title: Facing US export controls, China's DeepSeek plans to make its own chips
ai.summary: China's DeepSeek AI company is developing plans to manufacture its own semiconductor chips in response to U.S. export restrictions. The strategy aims to reduce dependency on foreign chip suppliers, particularly Nvidia and Huawei, which have been subject to American export controls. This move reflects China's broader effort to achieve technological self-sufficiency in AI infrastructure amid escalating U.S.-China tech competition. While still in early stages, DeepSeek's chip development initiative signals a significant shift toward domestic semiconductor production for AI applications, potentially reshaping global AI hardware markets and intensifying geopolitical competition in artificial intelligence technology.

quantum.title: Researchers Reveal the Power of 'Quantum Proofs'
quantum.summary: Researchers have demonstrated that verifying solutions to certain computational problems inherently requires engaging with the complexity of the quantum world. This finding reveals fundamental limitations in classical verification methods and highlights the irreducible role of quantum mechanics in proof-checking systems. The research suggests that quantum properties cannot be bypassed when validating solutions to specific problem classes, establishing quantum mechanics as a necessary component of certain computational verification processes rather than merely an optional enhancement.

quantum.title: Using mechanical vibrations instead of magnetic memory for quantum computing
quantum.summary: Researchers at ETH Zurich are exploring mechanical vibrations as an alternative to magnetic memory for storing information in quantum computers. This approach addresses persistent limitations in quantum information storage by leveraging mechanical systems rather than traditional magnetic approaches. The research represents a significant shift in quantum computing architecture, potentially offering improved stability and coherence times for quantum information. This development could help overcome current bottlenecks in quantum computer performance and scalability.

quantum.title: BitGo unveils quantum risk management tools for Bitcoin wallets
quantum.summary: BitGo has introduced a comprehensive suite of quantum risk management tools designed for institutional Bitcoin wallets. These tools address emerging threats posed by quantum computing to cryptocurrency security infrastructure. The development reflects growing industry concern about quantum computing's potential to compromise current cryptographic standards that protect digital assets. BitGo's quantum risk management suite represents a proactive approach to safeguarding institutional cryptocurrency holdings against future quantum-enabled attacks.

quantum.title: Astrophysicists Puzzle Over Webb's New Universe
quantum.summary: The James Webb Space Telescope has revealed unexpected observations of early black holes and galaxies that contradict existing cosmological models. Scientists have developed numerous new theories to explain these anomalous findings, but determining which explanations are correct remains challenging. The discoveries suggest fundamental gaps in current understanding of early universe formation and evolution. Researchers must now conduct further observations and analysis to validate competing theoretical frameworks and refine models of cosmic history.

quantum.title: For the First Time, a Cell Built From Scratch Grows and Divides
quantum.summary: Scientists have successfully created a synthetic cell from non-living materials that exhibits lifelike properties including growth and division capabilities. This breakthrough demonstrates proof-of-concept that laboratory-assembled components can be organized to produce cellular behavior previously thought exclusive to biological systems. The achievement represents a major milestone in synthetic biology, bridging the gap between chemistry and biology. The research has profound implications for understanding life's fundamental requirements and may enable future applications in biotechnology and medicine.

trump.title: U.S., Iran trade more strikes after Trump says ceasefire is "over"
trump.summary: President Trump declared the ceasefire with Iran "over," prompting escalated military exchanges between the two nations. The U.S. launched a second night of strikes on Wednesday, with Iran responding in kind. This development marks a significant escalation in ongoing tensions and represents a critical moment in Trump administration foreign policy, as the fragile negotiating process with Iran faces renewed strain following the president's unilateral decision to terminate the ceasefire agreement.

trump.title: Trump fires Election Assistance Commission leaders
trump.summary: President Trump terminated the remaining leaders of the U.S. Election Assistance Commission, raising significant concerns about election oversight ahead of midterm elections. The terminations follow Trump administration advocacy to modify vote-by-mail requirements and ongoing investigations into the 2020 election outcome. Critics have expressed deep concern about these actions, viewing them as part of broader efforts to interfere with electoral processes and undermine independent election administration.

trump.title: Travellers react as Florida airport renamed after Trump
trump.summary: Palm Beach International Airport was officially renamed President Donald J. Trump International Airport on July 9, 2026. The renaming represents a significant honor for the former and current president, with the airport serving as a major transportation hub in South Florida. Travellers and airport users have reacted to the name change, which reflects the airport's location in Trump's home state and his continued prominence in American politics and public life.

trump.title: Trump wants a Supreme Court do-over on birthright citizenship. Here's why it pro...
trump.summary: President Trump is seeking a Supreme Court reconsideration of birthright citizenship policy, indicating his desire to revisit the Court's recent decision on the matter. Trump-appointed Justice Brett Kavanaugh disagreed with the majority's decision, suggesting potential divisions among Trump's judicial appointees on this contentious constitutional issue. The push for a do-over reflects Trump's ongoing efforts to reshape immigration and citizenship policy through judicial channels.

trump.title: Work on Trump's E Jean Carroll defamation case divides Sullivan & Cromwell
trump.summary: Major law firm Sullivan & Cromwell initially committed to remaining neutral on President Trump's appeal of sex-abuse and defamation cases brought by E. Jean Carroll, but reversed course after being approached by Trump's personal lawyer. The firm's decision to become involved in the high-profile litigation has created internal divisions among partners. This development highlights the ongoing legal challenges Trump faces and the complexities surrounding legal representation in politically sensitive cases.
